q: What does an Asset event reference, and how does a reader reach the Entity it descends from?
oracle: An Asset references exactly its Manifestation. It never references an Entity directly. The Entity is reached by reading up the chain, Asset to Manifestation to Entity.

q: Which parts of AEMS must an event follow to be compliant, and which parts are optional?
oracle: Compliance is the four event kinds, the three parent references (Manifestation to at least one Entity, Asset to its Manifestation, State to its Asset), and addressability by kind, publisher key and d tag. Everything an event carries (tags, property names, namespaces, transfer patterns) is an optional convention.

q: What kind numbers do AEMS events use, and what tag encodes the parent reference?
oracle: Neither is pinned yet. Examples use named placeholders. The answer must not give a concrete kind number as AEMS's. If the docs state a constraint, it is that the kinds will be Nostr addressable kinds (30000-39999).

q: Can a player publish an Asset for an item they never earned? What in AEMS stops this?
oracle: Yes, anyone can sign any Asset. Nothing in the protocol stops it. Every event is a claim. A receiving game or community judges it by its provenance, and witnessing or reputation are ecosystem services. This is the intended design, not a gap.

q: Why doesn't AEMS prevent duplication or enforce scarcity?
oracle: AEMS provides authenticity by provenance, not scarcity. Copying is free; a false claim of origin is exposed by the signed chain. Physical reality is the reference: it bundles no scarcity enforcer into a game object, and enforcing scarcity would need monetary-grade consensus.

q: Is the Master Sword an Entity or a Manifestation?
oracle: `master-sword` can be an Entity: an authored concept is still an Entity, and its author's signature is where convergence concentrates. Breath of the Wild's Master Sword is a Manifestation (e.g. `botw:master-sword`) that references `master-sword` and `sword`. The answer must not say authored or trademarked concepts cannot be Entities.

q: Where do classification tags such as category, type, or game go: on the Entity or the Manifestation? Is `healing-item` a good Entity name?
oracle: On the Manifestation. An Entity carries only its naming (d, name, description). `healing-item` is a use classification, not an object-identity, so it is not a good Entity name.

q: Is the french-52 deck the canonical set of playing-card Entities that everyone should use? Should card Entities use `stdcard:` d-tags?
oracle: No. Nothing is canonical or blessed; the deck is an ecosystem artifact whose fidelity is unverified. There is no standard namespace; a bare unprefixed d (e.g. `ace-spades`) is the convention for a naming meant to be broadly shared.

q: I publish ten State events for one Asset, reusing the same d tag. Can a reader later retrieve all ten as the Asset's history?
oracle: Not reliably. These are addressable events; relays need keep only the latest and may discard older versions. History exists only where someone archived it, or if the publisher gives each State a distinct address.

q: Who signs a State event? If two different keys publish State for the same Asset, which is the current State?
oracle: The kernel does not fix the signer. Each signer's latest State is that signer's claim. When several keys publish State for one Asset, the reader chooses whose claim to honor. There is no single protocol-defined current State across signers.

q: Does an AEMS event's timestamp prove when it was created?
oracle: No. created_at is chosen by the signer and is part of the claim. Proof of age needs outside witnesses (e.g. a third party's signed reference or a timestamp attestation). A reference by event id proves only that the parent existed before the child.

q: Are AEMS events guaranteed to persist forever once published?
oracle: No. Nostr guarantees no persistence. An event lasts while some relay or archive keeps a copy. What Nostr does give is that anyone can re-host a signed event without the author, and it still verifies; no particular host is needed.

q: How do I give my Asset to another player?
oracle: AEMS does not define transfer yet: the kernel has no transfer rule and no transfer convention exists. Because an Asset's address includes the owner's key, the recipient would publish a new Asset; linking it to the old one is a convention still to be written.

q: Can I ask a relay for every Manifestation whose category tag is `weapon`?
oracle: Not with standard Nostr filters: relays index only single-letter tags. A multi-letter tag like category can be filtered only after fetching, by the client. (Docs may name a single-letter alternative.)

q: Does RUNS import AEMS data, and does a RUNS game need AEMS?
oracle: No. AEMS is independent and needs no other protocol, and RUNS works without AEMS. They meet only at optional seams: build time (Manifestation data baked into a build) and load/save (Asset and State). An AEMS Asset is not the runtime object a game updates each frame.
